# Getting started with Google Gemini for everyday life

> **In short:** Go to gemini.google.com, sign in with your Google Account, type your request in the text box at the bottom, and click **Submit**. Keep chatting in the same conversation to refine the answer, and double-check anything important, because Google says Gemini can make mistakes.

Gemini is Google's AI assistant. You can ask it to plan a meal, draft an email, or explain a topic in plain words, and it writes an answer for you. This guide follows Google's own Gemini help pages and walks you through your first conversation.

## Before you start
-   **A Google Account.** Google's help page says you need a personal Google Account (or a work or school account your organization has set up for Gemini). Work accounts also require you to be 18 or older.
-   **A device with internet.** A computer, tablet, or phone.
-   **No paid plan for these steps.** You can try everything below with a personal Google Account.
-   **About 6 minutes.**

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and sign in
Open your web browser and go to **gemini.google.com**. If you aren't signed in yet, sign in with your Google Account.

On a phone, Google also offers the Gemini mobile app for Android and for iPhone and iPad. Google's help pages have separate setup instructions for each.

**If it looks different:** If Google asks you to review terms or settings the first time, read them and continue. Screens can change between versions, but the text box for your request is the part you need.

You'll know it worked when you see a text box at the bottom of the page where you can type.

## Step 2 — Write your request like a sentence
In the AI world, the request you type is called a **prompt**. Gemini is built on an **LLM (large language model)**: software trained on large amounts of text so it can understand your request and write a reply in its own words.

That's why full sentences with details work better than a few keywords. Say who it's for, what you need, and any limits, such as time or budget.

💬 Example (keywords only): "Best parks in Chicago with barbecues"
💬 Example (a full prompt): "I am planning a family picnic in Chicago. Recommend three parks with free barbecues, shade, and nearby parking."

You'll know it worked when you have a prompt ready that says what you want, for whom, and with which limits.

## Step 3 — Send your first prompt
Click the text box at the bottom of the page and type your prompt. Google's help page says you can also add a file or an image if you want. Then click **Submit** to send it.

Gemini writes its answer above the text box.

You'll know it worked when Gemini's answer appears on the screen.

💬 Example: "I have leftover pumpkin, baby spinach, and pasta in my cupboard. Can you suggest a simple dinner recipe I can make in 20 minutes using these ingredients?"

## Step 4 — Follow up in the same chat
If the first answer isn't quite right, don't start over. Type a follow-up in the same text box, and Gemini takes the earlier messages in this conversation into account.

When you want a fresh topic, Google's help page says to click **New chat** at the top left (if you don't see it, open the **Menu** first).

You'll know it worked when Gemini changes or expands its previous answer based on your follow-up.

💬 Example follow-up prompts:
-   "Can you make that recipe dairy-free?"
-   "Can you write out a quick shopping list for any extra ingredients I might need?"

## Common mistakes
-   **Typing only a few keywords:** "pasta recipe" gets you a very general answer.
    *   **The fix:** Add details, such as "easy vegetarian pasta for one person, ready in 15 minutes." The more context you give, the more useful the answer.
-   **Starting a new chat for every change:** A new chat doesn't continue your earlier conversation.
    *   **The fix:** Ask your follow-up in the same chat, such as "Can you make that shorter?" or "Now turn that into an email."
-   **Trusting important facts without checking:** Google's help page says Gemini can make mistakes and that you shouldn't rely on its responses as professional advice. AI can **hallucinate (confidently state something that sounds real but is wrong)**.
    *   **The fix:** Double-check important details, such as health information, opening hours, travel times, or rules, with a reliable source.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** Plan a weekly menu, draft a polite reply to an invitation, brainstorm gift ideas, or get help wording a difficult message.
-   **For your business or work:** Get a first draft of an email, brainstorm headlines, or ask for a plain-language explanation of a topic. Check the result before you use it.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Don't worry about writing the "perfect" prompt. Type naturally, then ask Gemini to try again or be more specific.

## Try it now
Go to **gemini.google.com**, sign in, and type this prompt:

*"Suggest three relaxing weekend day-trip ideas starting from my local area, including one spot for lunch."* (Replace "my local area" with your town or neighborhood.)
